units.en: Han had held off Zhenjie in the south and defeated Xiancheng in the north. He had to be won by conciliation, not crushed by force. In the end he brought the region back to the empire. Was that not wise policy?
units.literal: Moreover Han resisted Zhenjie in the south and defeated Xiancheng in the north; he should have been won by kindness and could not be subdued by force; in the end he caused the region to return to the state — was this not a sound plan?

units.zh: 向討之，即為劇賊矣。
units.en: Had the court attacked him instead, he would have become a far more dangerous rebel.
units.literal: Had they attacked him instead, he would have become a fierce bandit.

units.zh: 然事佛僥福，朋勢取容，非君子之道焉。
units.en: Yet in seeking fortune through Buddhism and currying favor through factions he fell short of the way of a true gentleman.
units.literal: Yet in serving Buddhism to seek fortune and currying favor through factional power he did not follow the way of the gentleman.

units.zh: 贊曰：玄宗失德，祿山肆逆。
units.en: The encomium reads: Xuanzong lost his virtue, and An Lushan rose in rebellion.
units.literal: The encomium says: Xuanzong lost virtue and Lushan wildly rebelled.

units.zh: 見素竭節，諸公協力。
units.en: Jiansu gave his utmost, and these men worked together in the state's service.
units.literal: Jiansu exhausted his integrity and the various lords joined their strength.

units.zh: 硃泚反，李懷光又叛河中，使其將趙貴先築壘於同州，紓來奔奉天，向領州務。
units.en: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huaiguang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong prefecture; Li Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
units.literal: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huaiguang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong Prefecture; Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.

units.zh: 李涵，高平王道立曾孫。
units.en: Li Han was the great-grandson of Daoli, Prince of Gaoping.
units.literal: Li Han was the great-grandson of Daoli, Prince of Gaoping.

units.zh: 涵簡素恭慎，有名宗室，累授贊善大夫、兼侍御史。
units.en: Han was plain, frugal, respectful, and cautious, a well-known member of the imperial clan who was repeatedly appointed gentleman attendant and concurrent palace censor.
units.literal: Han was plain, frugal, respectful, and cautious, a noted member of the imperial clan, and was repeatedly appointed gentleman attendant and concurrent palace censor.

units.zh: 涵與朔方留後杜鴻漸，草箋具朔方兵馬招集之勢，軍資倉儲庫物之數，鹹推涵宗枝之英，純厚忠信，乃令涵奉箋至平涼謁見。
units.en: Han and Du Hongjian, acting commissioner of Shuofang, drafted a memorial detailing the forces being gathered in Shuofang and the quantities of military supplies in store. All praised Han as an outstanding member of the imperial clan, pure, generous, loyal, and trustworthy, and Han was sent to present the memorial at Pingliang.
units.literal: Han and Du Hongjian, acting commissioner of Shuofang, drafted a memorial setting forth the strength of Shuofang troops being gathered, and the numbers of military supplies, granaries, and storehouses; all praised Han as an outstanding branch of the imperial clan, pure, generous, loyal, and trustworthy, and so Han was ordered to present the memorial at Pingliang for audience.

units.zh: 涵敷奏明辯，動合事機，肅宗大悅，除右司員外郎，累至司封郎中、宗正少卿。
units.en: Han spoke clearly and persuasively, and his words always matched the moment. Emperor Suzong was greatly pleased and appointed him outer office director in the Right Secretariat. He later rose to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites and Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
units.literal: Han presented his case clearly and persuasively, and his words always matched the moment; Emperor Suzong was greatly pleased and appointed him outer office director in the Right Secretariat, and he rose in time to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites and Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

units.zh: 朔方節度郭子儀奏為關內鹽池判官。
units.en: Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, recommended him as salt-pond administrator for the region within the passes.
units.literal: Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, memorialized that he be made salt-pond administrator within the passes.

units.zh: 父少康，宋州刺史。
units.en: His father Shaokang had served as prefect of Songzhou.
units.literal: His father Shaokang was prefect of Songzhou.

units.zh: 肅宗北幸平涼，未有所適。
units.en: When Emperor Suzong went north to Pingliang, the court had not yet chosen its next refuge.
units.literal: Emperor Suzong went north to Pingliang and had not yet decided where to go.

units.zh: 陜虢觀察使李齊運表置幕府。
units.en: Observation commissioner Li Qiyun of Shan-Guo placed him on staff.
units.literal: Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of Shan-Guo, memorialized to place him on his staff.

units.zh: 齊運入為京兆尹，表奉先主簿，拜監察御史，坐累免。
units.en: When Qiyun became Jingzhao magistrate, he recommended Ning as Fengxian chief clerk; Ning became Attending Censor but was dismissed for a fault.
units.literal: When Qiyun became metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, he recommended him as chief clerk of Fengxian; he was made Attending Censor and dismissed for an offense.

units.zh: 既而郭英乂代適，以厭人望，奏署秘書郎，兼雒令，以疾免。
units.en: When Guo Yingyi succeeded Gao Shi, he placated public opinion by appointing Ban Hong secretary and magistrate of Luoyang, though illness soon forced Hong to leave office.
units.literal: Before long Guo Yingyi replaced Shi; to sate public expectation, he memorialized appointing Hong secretary and concurrently magistrate of Luo; he was dismissed for illness.

units.zh: 坦與李絳葉議，以為：「西城張仁願所築，制匈奴上策。
units.en: Tan and Li Jiang jointly argued: "The western city Zhang Renyuan built is the best strategy for holding the northern frontier.
units.literal: Tan and Li Jiang jointly deliberated and considered: "The western city built by Zhang Renyuan is the supreme strategy for controlling the northern nomads.

units.zh: 城當磧口，居虜要沖，美水豐草，邊防所利。
units.en: It sits at the desert pass on the enemy's vital route, with fine water and lush grass—an ideal border fortress.
units.literal: The city sits at the desert pass, occupies the enemy's vital crossing, has fine water and lush grass, and is advantageous for border defense.

units.zh: 今河流之決，不過退就二三里，奈何舍萬代安永之策，徇一時省費之謀？
units.en: The river breach requires retreating only two or three li. Why abandon a plan secure for ten thousand generations for a moment's savings?
units.literal: Now the river's breach requires retreating only two or three li—how can one abandon a plan secure for ten thousand generations and follow a scheme to save costs for a moment?

units.zh: 況天德故城僻處確瘠，其北枕山，與河絕遠，烽候警備，不相統接。
units.en: Moreover old Tiede City lies remote on stony barren ground. Mountains press close to the north, it is far from the river, and its beacon posts do not connect with the rest of the border defense.
units.literal: Moreover the old Tiede City lies remote in stony barrenness; to its north mountains press close, it is utterly far from the river, and beacon posts and watch stations do not connect in unified defense.

units.zh: 虜之唐突，勢無由知，是無故而蹙國二百里，非所利也。」
units.en: Nomad raids would go undetected. This would shrink the border two hundred li for no good reason."
units.literal: When the barbarians raid, there is no way to know—this would without cause shrink the realm by two hundred li; it is not advantageous."

units.zh: 元和八年，西受降城為河徙浸毀，宰相李吉甫請移兵於天德故城。
units.en: In Yuanhe 8 Western Shouxiang City was damaged when the river shifted. Chancellor Li Jifu proposed moving the garrison to old Tiede City.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe, Western Shouxiang City was damaged by a shifting river; Chancellor Li Jifu requested moving the garrison to the old Tiede City.

units.zh: 是歲，賈至為侍郎，建言歲方艱歉，舉人赴省者，兩都試之。
units.en: That year Jia Zhi served as vice-minister of rites and proposed that, given the year's hardship and scarcity, candidates traveling to the capital should be examined in both capitals instead.
units.literal: That year, Jia Zhi was vice-minister and proposed that since the year was one of hardship and dearth, candidates coming to the capital should be examined in both capitals.

units.zh: 詔給事中李棲筠、李廙、尚書左丞賈至、京兆尹兼御史大夫嚴武議。
units.en: The emperor ordered palace attendants Li Qiyun and Li Yi, left assistant minister Jia Zhi, and Jingzhao intendant and concurrent censor-in-chief Yan Wu to deliberate.
units.literal: An edict ordered Palace Attendants Li Qiyun and Li Yi, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Jia Zhi, and Jingzhao Intendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief Yan Wu to deliberate.

units.zh: 兩都試人自此始。
units.en: Dual-capital examinations began from this time.
units.literal: Examination of candidates in both capitals began from this point.

candidateDisclosure: These are bounded name-index headers, not primary-evidence proofs of equivalence or difference. Full immutable registry and posting counts/fingerprints remain sealed on host. No candidate may be merged or separated by this report. Uninspected aliases or overflow remain uncertain.

reviews.reason: Specific source-based reason. Hold a concrete wrong actor or false existing merge. Preserve uncertainty about cross-chapter equivalence.

instructions: Review every case and every target local person. Quote the primary Chinese for each target and the retained canonical anchor. Confirm actual individual, supported chapter attribution, and accepted membership; hold contradictions. Keep unresolvedIdentity true when proposed, including small candidate buckets and overflow. Omitted names are unreviewed uncertainty, never separation evidence. No positive merges, no all-pairs comparisons, no recursive external chapter completion. Return the closed required report only. Supply definite English repairs separately with complete exact before/after, source reason, both fields and repetitions; do not silently ignore them.
